why: CLAUDE.md: IPs live ONLY in the host registry, and consumers resolve by NAME. A literal in
live code is an address that cannot follow a lease. But a few places genuinely cannot use a
name: the bootstrap that RESOLVES names cannot resolve one before it has the registry; a
self-signed cert's SAN is an IP because guest devices connect by IP; and container-internal
podman addresses have no fleet DNS at all. For those, a small, NAMED, EXPIRING allowlist is the
AN ALLOWLIST WITHOUT EXPIRY IS A PERMANENT HOLE. Every entry carries `expires` and
`re_derivation`. Past its expiry an entry is a FAILURE, not a warning: the fence goes red and
someone has to look again. `re_derivation` is the command that recovers the value, so a reader
can CHECK the literal rather than trust it.
CORRECTED 2026-08-01: the two pre-existing entries' re_derivation pointed at
`viewer/host_registry.json` (which does not exist) and a `boxes[].id` field (the real field is
`name`). A re-derivation command that errors is worse than none - it looks checkable and is not.
Both now name the real file and field. Ten entries were added the same day when the IP->DNS
remediation turned 29 live literals into names: what remained are the addresses a name genuinely
cannot replace, each with the reason it must stay and the date it must be looked at again.

rules.expiry_is_a_failure: an entry past `expires` fails the fence; it does not warn
rules.no_open_ended_entries: `expires` is required on every entry and may not be null or 'never'
rules.re_derivation_is_required: an allowlisted literal a reader cannot recompute is a literal nobody can check

literals.why: the WireGuard mesh gateway. The bootstrap dials it to reach the registry; it cannot resolve a name before it has the registry that resolves names.
the chip's mesh address, used only by the sanctioned bootstrap probe.

THE CHIP'S CURRENT DHCP LAN LEASE, dialled by the bootstrap DNS resolver before any name can be resolved. It is NOT declarable (the _lan_dynamic_law: a lease is never pinned in the registry), so it cannot be swapped for a name here. This entry exists to be RETIRED by the operator's overlay-plane move (plan O2/O3: dial the chip via the stable tailscale overlay 100.100.188.48 that THINKER can reach, and allowlist THAT instead). Its expiry is the deadline for that co-signed decision - never allowlist .121 again past it, because pinning a lease is the exact trap the fence exists to catch.

the chip's current LAN lease, written into the Windows NRPT rule that routes *.uni-lab.local to the chip's dnsmasq - the one resolver that cannot itself be addressed by the name it serves. Same lease-not-declarable case as infra.cjs; retired by the same operator overlay-plane move (O4).

mc.uni-lab.local - the Minecraft world host, in the NRPT routing rule. Declared in the zone (production/dns/uni-lab.local.hosts) and recoverable by name; kept as a literal only because an NRPT rule maps a name-suffix to a resolver IP by IP.

the SAN of the studio's self-signed cert for the camera gateway. Guest contributors open https://<thinker>:8443/ BY IP (the cert's SAN is the IP; a DNS name would cert-mismatch on a guest device that may not resolve the private zone), so the literal is intrinsic to the cert. The primary source is still channels.json { host }; this is the fallback SAN.
the camera-gateway URL printed in the bring-up banner for LAN devices. IP-addressed to match the cert SAN above (same guest-connects-by-IP reason).

node2's LAN address advertised as a WebRTC ICE host candidate by the relay's MediaMTX (webrtcAdditionalHosts). ICE candidates are literal addresses by protocol - a browser cannot ICE against a name. node2 is declared in the registry; the operator applies this yaml change on the live relay (plan O5).

the relay container's current podman-bridge IP (RELAY_RTMP/SRT defaults). The default 'podman' bridge has no aardvark-dns, so container-name resolution fails and this is addressed by IP. NO fleet DNS name exists for a container-internal address. Overridable via env; the durable fix (the file's own comment) is a custom podman network with DNS. System-2, authored-not-run.
the podman bridge GATEWAY, named in a docstring explaining why cam reads address the gateway not a container IP (container IPs move across restarts). Container-plane address, no fleet DNS.
the relay container IP the OBS entrypoint pushes to. Same container-internal, no-fleet-DNS case as build_scenes.py. System-2.
the podman bridge gateway the pubgate's WHIP proxy reaches the relay through. Container-plane address, no fleet DNS. System-2.

expiry_is_a_hard_failure: EVERY ENTRY HERE EXPIRES, AND AN EXPIRED ENTRY IS A HARD FAILURE OF viewer/verify_ip_fence.cjs -- not a warning. The 2026-10-30 horizon is deliberate: it is the deadline by which the operator's overlay-plane move (O2/O3/O4 for the two .121 lease entries) and the podman-network-DNS follow-up (the 10.88.0.x entries) must be done or consciously re-dated. Do not silently bump these; re-derive with each entry's command, or let it expire and look again.
